Two South African engineers set free

By: Annalise Lubbe | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After having spent two harrowing years in prison in Equatorial Guinea two innocent South African engineers are finally home. We bring you their story.

Unique Selling Point:
It was the moment Peter Huxham and Frik Potgieter have been waiting for ... .to step back on South African soil at Lanseria Airport where their families have been waiting anxiously. It was an emotional welcome for the two engineers who have not seen their loved ones since their illegal detention in a high security prison in Equatorial Guinea in February 2023.

Their release follows a pardon from the President of Equatorial Guinea. This brings an end to a harrowing ordeal of anguish, uncertainty, and unwavering efforts by many to secure their freedom.


Summary:
It is a story of two men who have spent two years and four months in a prison for a crime they did not commit. The emotional, physical and mental toll it took on both Frik and Peter is beyond words. How do you come to terms with the thought that your faith lies in the hands of a government whose judicial system is corrupt? What led to their eventual release was a presidential pardon which proves that they were innocent from the beginning.

During those dark days and nights their loved ones lived only in their memory. With the exception of a handful of brief telephone calls, the only connection they had was with the local doctor and their legal representative of the company they worked for. The men lost weight and the worry lines ran deep on their faces. Both are on chronic medication and the poor diet in prison have added to their weight loss.

We covered the story of their arrest, sentencing and imprisonment. Now we bring you the story of how the men coped in prison, how their families continued their unfailing support and calling for their release and the eventual release from prison.

We take you into the homes of Peter Huxham who, while in prison, proposed to his partner Kathy, who accepted. Kathy, who never gave up hope, washed and ironed Peter’s clothes every week and packed it away for the day he returns.

Frik Potgieter’s wife Sonja was part of the support group who sat in countless meetings with DIRCO and on the street during the protest.

Timeline:
Frik Potgieter and Peter Huxham were arrested in their hotel room in Malabo in Equatorial Guinea on 9 February 2023 on trumped up drug charges and subsequently imprisoned. The two men were arrested two days after South African courts seized the super yacht belonging to the Equatorial Guinean Vice President, and just shortly after two of his Cape Town luxury homes were impounded. The seizures followed a separate court ruling in South Africa that had nothing to do with Frik and Peter.

The two men appeared in court on 22 June 2023 charged with illegal drug trafficking. The court case was a farce as no credible evidence, witnesses, or expert testimonies were presented to the court by the State, nor was any proof presented that the alleged drugs were found on Peter or Frik, or that indeed they were drugs. It was alleged that the drugs were found in their luggage, but this was not ture. Their luggage, combination-locked and unopened, was still in their rooms five days later when their employer collected them in the presence of hotel management and the local police.

On 29 June 2023 they were found guilty of illegal drug trafficking. Peter and Frik were sentenced each for 12 years in a high security prison in Mongomo, Equatorial Guinea in a prison reserved for political prisoners. They were ordered to pay USD $5 million each in damages, and additional fines to be shared between them. The sentences were based on outdated penalties for the alleged crimes indicating an unsettling departure from the country’s Criminal Code.

In July 2024, the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found that their imprisonment was arbitrary, unlawful, and in breach of multiple international human rights obligations. The UN also, at the time, called for their immediate release as their physical and mental health deteriorated, and their families were left in anguish.

In October 2024, the South African Parliament passed a unanimous motion demanding urgent action to secure their release. Despite this, Frik and Peter remained in prison in Equatorial Guinea. At the same time the families appealed to the South African government (DIRCO) for urgent intervention and the Presidency to push for Peter and Frik’s release. In a letter to President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, the president of Equatorial Guinea, the families pleaded for clemency. They appealed to him directly as a father and a devout Catholic to have mercy.

To support their fight for justice the families turned to social media, calling on the immediate release of Frik and Peter. The petition was signed by 16,000 signatures from around the world.
A peaceful protests was staged in Cape Town at the Africa Energy Week which was attended by the South African Minister of International Relations, Minister Ronald Lamola, and his UK counterpart, Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs, the Rt Hon David Lammy to find an urgent solution to Frik and Peter’s ongoing detention in Equatorial Guinea.

On Human Rights Day, 21 March 2025 the families continued to call on the government for diplomatic efforts to secure the men’s release from unlawful detention and imploring the President of Equatorial Guinea to grant the men clemency.

Then finally, on 21 June 2025 the families of Frik and Peter confirmed that the men have been released and are at home. No media was invited to cover their arrival at Lanseria Airport as there was still a certain amount of doubt that perhaps something could go wrong.

Frik and Peter were pardoned by the President of Equatorial Guinea: an act recognising that no crime had been committed by the two men and that they are innocent and their rights should be restored. On the same day of the release a tweet from his son, Teodoro Nguema Obiang, was posted: “Once again, His Excellency the President of the Republic has demonstrated to the world his humanism, solidarity, and reconciliation, the values that embody him, by granting pardons to two South African citizens convicted of drug trafficking”.

Peter and Frik’s attorneys in Equatorial Guinea are currently lodging appeals on several issues, including the court process, the verdict, unlawful sentence of imprisonment, and the amounts that they have to pay in damages, fines and legal costs.

The story
In this exclusive TV interview we will hear the stories of Peter and Frik and what they endured during these 2,4 years in maximum prison and how they coped.
We will hear the heartfelt stories from their wives and what it was like living without your partner for so long

We will briefly summarise the past two Carte Blanche stories we covered on the two engineers, how they were arrested, imprisoned, and the tit-for-tat political game played by the son of the president that caused them to be thrown in jail.

FINAL BROADCAST Script: Engineers set free
Date: 20 July 2025
Duration: 11 minutes 20 seconds

UPS Masa: A local news channel says they were in possession of bags of white powder.
UPSound Frederik Potgieter, “No, no, never in my life”
Peter Huxham: “It’s not mine.”

Peter Huxham - Cameraman arrived with a camera, and on it was TV GE, which is TV, Guinea Equatorial, and I didn't know it was for us. I thought this was just a mistake and it'll be resolved. I've got nothing to do with drugs. Why would I be concerned?


Pause


VO1: But Peter Huxham should have been concerned. That night in a hotel room in the west African dictatorship of Equatorial Guinea would be the start of a nightmare lasting more than two years.

Archive Visuals

VO2: He and another South African, Frederik Potgieter, known as Frik, were questioned by local police and shown bags of white powder.
That night was the first time the two had met.

Frik Potgieter: Ek het hom geken van geen kant af nie. (I didn’t recognise him.) So ek het net gesien daarso sit nog 'n wit ou op die bank. (I only saw another white person sitting on a bench.)

Peter Huxham: Eventually I said, Well, it's not mine. It's not my stuff! And the question he was asking me was: “are you saying the police are lying?”

VO3: Equatorial Guinea has been ruled by the same man since 1979, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo. He’s known for ruling with an iron fist. It’s reported political dissidents were sent to one of the most notorious prisons in the world – Black Beach.
PAUSE That’s where Peter and Frik were held.

UPS Newzroom Afrika
South Africans have been released from a prison in Equatorial Guinea where they were detained for more than two-and-a-half years.


UPS Frik Potgieter: Dankie Here vir die dag. (Thank you, Lord, for this day) Dankie vir die ondersteuning wat U vir my gegee het….(Thank you, Lord, for the support you have given me.)

VO4: Having been arrested in early February 2023, Frik and Peter are now home. They were released after years of negotiations at every possible level, and their OWN story - told on television for the first time – suggests they paid a brutal price for a vendetta that had nothing to do with them.

PAUSE

VO5: It began with the arrest and quickly snowballed.

Peter Huxham: When we arrived in the courthouse, we knew, I can't tell you how we knew somebody would be endangered by that. But we knew, so we had the knowledge that this is a diplomatic event.


Pause


VO6 The diplomatic event Peter is referring to unfolded ten years before their imprisonment. Another South African, Daniel Janse van Rensburg, was arrested after a business deal with a relative of the President’s son went sour. He was thrown into Black Beach where he would spend four years before his release. Years later, Janse van Rensburg successfully sued, and assets in Cape Town belonging to Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo’s son were attached by the court.
PAUSE
It’s here that the seeds were sown for Peter and Frik’s ordeal.
PAUSE
It’s believed they were used as bargaining chips for the return of those assets which included two luxury houses.


Pause

VO7 The court found Frik and Peter guilty of TRAFFICKING AND THE ILLICIT POSSESSION OF DRUGS and their more than 24 months in prison began, first being sent to Black Beach.

Frik Potgieter: Toe ons daar aan kom en die staldeur nou oopmaak, (When we arrived there, and they opened the steel door,) toe's daar seker, ek skat tussen twee en driehonderd mense daar binne-in. (an estimated 200 or 300 people were inside.)

Peter Huxham: One of the guards. He took us to one side. He said, You just need to be calm. You need to try and not show any fear.


Frik: Toe’t ek geskrik. Toe sceme ek ek gaan nie môre oggend hier uitkom nie. (That’s when I got a fright. I thought, “Tomorrow, I’m not going to come out of here.) Dis my laaste aand hierso. (This is my last night here.”)


VO8 But worse was yet to come.

LINK: From notorious Black Beach Peter and Frik were moved to another high security prison. They were blindfolded and handcuffed and taken to what they called the hole.

VO9 The prison in an area called Mongomo, while not as well-known as Black Beach, was arguably more sinister – housing political prisoners and criminals of the worst kind.

PAUSE

VO10 The men spent 6 weeks in solitary confinement.

Frik Potgieter - Die selle is baie klein. Die ligte brand permanent in die selle. (The cells are very small. The lights are permanently on.) Daarso is niks indication van of dit dag of nag is nie.(There is… no indication of day or night.)
VO11 The months came and went


PAUSE


UPS: Kathy McConnachie: We haven’t spoken to our men in months.
Sonja Potgieter: Yah please, if you can just help us.


PAUSE


VO12 Back in South Africa their families lobbied the government and parliament. They wrote letters, staged silent protests, and drew attention to their cause on social media.

UPS: We’re going to use Parliamentary diplomacy to do what’s needed in this case.

VO13 In June last year, the United Nations declared Peter and Frik ‘s incarceration a human rights violation.
Frik Potgieter: Dit het vir ons baie hoop gegee en baie moed gegee. (It gave us a lot of hope and courage) Ons het nog steeds aan die een kant getwyfel, want wat gaan die UN vir EG doen?(We still had our doubts, because what can the UN do to EG?)
PAUSE

UPS: Sonja Potgieter: Hier is die eerste boek wat ek geskryf het.

VO14 Frik’s wife, Sonja, kept a diary to record things she could no longer share with him.


Sonja Potgieter: Ons het nie geweet hoe lank hy daar gaan wees nie (We didn’t know how long he was going to be there.) So ek het begin skryf vir hom…ek het nou al 5 boeke vol geskryf. (So, I started writing to him…I have written 5 books already)


Erin: Het dit jou gehelp? (Did that help you?)


Sonja: Dis al hoe dit my gehelp het om hom net te begin vertel van die dag (It’s the only thing that helped me, to tell him about my day.) want dan voel dit vir my asof ek met hom praat. (That made me feel like I was talking to him.)


VO15 the men were allowed only a handful of phone calls.
Frik: Dit was seker tien, vyf minute die oproep. (It was probably ten- or five- minute phone calls.) Maar ons het amper meer gehuil as wat ons gepraat het. (But we cried more than talked.)
SHORT PAUSE
Erin: 16;47;28 Wat het jy die meeste gemis van die huis af? (What did you miss most about home?)
Frik: Om 'n deur te kan oopmaak en te kan uitstap, buite toe. (To open a door and walk outside.) Ja, en human, human interaction. Net 'n drukkie of 'n smile of wat ook al. (Yes, and human interaction. Just a hug or a smile or something.)
PAUSE


UPSound: Sonja: Dit klop so vinning want jy is in hegtenis geneem. (It’s beating so fast. You have been arrested.) Wat nou, hoekom? (What now? Why?) Maar ek is dankbaar dis verby. (But I’m thankful it’s over) Ons is deur alles. (We went through it all).


PAUSE


UPSound: Peter: I wish I was there to just hold you and tell you: “We’ll be ok and that we will all as a family get through this”.

VO16 Kathy McConnachie has been with Peter for 32 years.

Kathy: My first main concern was his health. Because I knew he depended on his antidepressant and if he didn’t have those he wouldn’t manage.


Peter Huxham: It was extremely difficult. I mean, it got to a point where I lost control.


VO17 Medication did eventually arrive, but Peter still had very bad days.


Peter: And it got to a point where in November, I had blood running down my face from banging my head on the cell door, and the supervisors were shouting at each other. What are they going to do?


VO18 Ironically, because it seemed certain Peter and Frik were being used as political pawns, their captors needed to keep them in reasonable health.


Peter; They eventually got me to the infirmary, and I think that's still when I said to the supervisor, just kill me now. Just kill me.

Erin: And you meant it?

Peter Huxham: Yes, absolutely. At that moment in time, I prayed. I prayed, God, take me.


UPS protest march


VO19 On the 21st of March, South Africa’s Human Rights Day, the families renewed their call for the government to intervene and secure Peter and Frik’s release.

PAUSE

Three months later they were pardoned.

Peter: We just sat there like it's as if all the tension and all the anxiety of the last 28 months just sort of disappeared, and you're just relieved.

UP music


LINK: It was the moment Peter and Frik had been longing for, to step back on South African soil with their families anxiously waiting for their return.

UPSOUND VIDEO


Erin: What was it like seeing her?

Peter Huxham: Just like nothing else mattered at that moment in time. Just that reconnection and that feeling, this person that you want to share your life with. You can’t live without her. I’ve realised that.

Kathy: I was crying. He was as happy as anything and he didn’t stop hugging me ... .and it was part of me that came home.

Up music
Frik: Toe kon ek, sien ek al die mense buite. ( I saw all the people outside.) Toe sien ek vir Sonja en vir Jolene (I saw Sonja and Jolene.) En toe ek afkom die trappe toe sien ek vir Frickie ook, my seun ook daarso staan. (And when I came down the stairs, I also saw Frikkie - my son - standing there.) Maar dit was overwhelming gewees, ja. (It was overwhelming.)
UPS - Frik, Jolene and Sonja in garden with dogs
Frik: Ja, so ek weet dis tyd wat mens probeer inhaal wat ek nie kan inhaal nie. (I’m trying to make up for lost time,) Maar om nuwe memories te skep, is al, en tyd te gee. (and to create new memories and to give it time.)
UPS


Erin: Now that he is home. What are the sweetest moments?

Kathy: Oh it is just sitting on the couch watching TV, holding my hand….Kath would you like a cup of coffee? That’s what I missed the most. So it’s Kath, coffee?

UPS Peter: I’d love to see this up close almost as much as I would like to see the pyramids.


VO21 Peter and Kathy plan to get married in October and then, a long awaited honeymoon in Europe


Pause

VO22 Frik and Sonja are looking forward to a road trip around the country and Namibia… they won’t go any further north than that.


Music up - Peter on bicycle

PROMO ONE
VO Two South African engineers spent more than 2 years in prison in Equatorial Guinea with no physical contact with family and only a handful of phone calls.
Upsound: Frik Potgieter: Toe ons daar aan kom en die staldeur nou oopmaak, (When we arrived there, and they opened the steel door,) toe's daar seker, ek skat tussen twee en driehonderd mense daar binne-in. (an estimated 200 or 300 people were inside.)

PROMO TWO
VO Locked behind bars in Equatorial Guinea in a confined space they spent two years in prison for a crime they did not commit
UPS: Frik Potgieter - Die selle is baie klein. Die ligte brand permanent in die selle.(The cells are small. The lights are permanently on.) Daarso is niks indication van of dit dag of nag is nie. (There is no indication of day or night.)

PROMO THREE
VO Two South African engineers….now finally home after 864 days in prison in Equatorial Guinea.
UPS: Peter Huxham - At that moment in time, I prayed. I prayed, God, take me. I don't want to be here.

A peaceful protests was staged in Cape Town at the Africa Energy Week which was attended by the South African Minister of International Relations, Minister Ronald Lamola, and his UK counterpart, Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs, the Rt Hon David Lammy to find an urgent solution to Frik and Peter’s ongoing detention in Equatorial Guinea. Frik and Peter were pardoned by the President of Equatorial Guinea: an act recognising that no crime had been committed by the two men and that they are innocent and their rights should be restored. On the same day of the release a tweet from his son, Teodoro Nguema Obiang, was posted: “Once again, His Excellency the President of the Republic has demonstrated to the world his humanism, solidarity, and reconciliation, the values that embody him, by granting pardons to two South African citizens convicted of drug trafficking”. Peter and Frik’s attorneys in Equatorial Guinea are currently lodging appeals on several issues, including the court process, the verdict, unlawful sentence of imprisonment, and the amounts that they have to pay in damages, fines and legal costs. The story In this exclusive TV interview we will hear the stories of Peter and Frik and what they endured during these 2,4 years in maximum prison and how they coped. We will hear the heartfelt stories from their wives and what it was like living without your partner for so long We will briefly summarise the past two Carte Blanche stories we covered on the two engineers, how they were arrested, imprisoned, and the tit-for-tat political game played by the son of the president that caused them to be thrown in jail. ___________________________________________________________________________ Extra Budget Items: Return flights George / CT x 3 Car hire x 2 days Case Study: Frik Potgieter Peter Huxham Sonja Potgieter Kathy McConnachie Other Footage Sources: Old Carte Blanche archives stories Hidden Camera: No Legal: Yes Reason for legal: The two men were in prison and eventually set free after a presidential pardon from Equatorial Guinea. Duration: 11 minutes 20 seconds UPS Masa: A local news channel says they were in possession of bags of white powder. UPSound Frederik Potgieter, “No, no, never in my life” Peter Huxham: “It’s not mine.” Peter Huxham - Cameraman arrived with a camera, and on it was TV GE, which is TV, Guinea Equatorial, and I didn't know it was for us. I thought this was just a mistake and it'll be resolved. I've got nothing to do with drugs. Why would I be concerned? Pause VO1: But Peter Huxham should have been concerned. That night in a hotel room in the west African dictatorship of Equatorial Guinea would be the start of a nightmare lasting more than two years. Archive Visuals VO2: He and another South African, Frederik Potgieter, known as Frik, were questioned by local police and shown bags of white powder. That night was the first time the two had met. Frik Potgieter: Ek het hom geken van geen kant af nie. (I didn’t recognise him.) So ek het net gesien daarso sit nog 'n wit ou op die bank. (I only saw another white person sitting on a bench.) Peter Huxham: Eventually I said, Well, it's not mine. It's not my stuff! And the question he was asking me was: “are you saying the police are lying?” VO3: Equatorial Guinea has been ruled by the same man since 1979, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo. He’s known for ruling with an iron fist. It’s reported political dissidents were sent to one of the most notorious prisons in the world – Black Beach. PAUSE That’s where Peter and Frik were held. UPS Newzroom Afrika South Africans have been released from a prison in Equatorial Guinea where they were detained for more than two-and-a-half years. UPS Frik Potgieter: Dankie Here vir die dag. (Thank you, Lord, for this day) Dankie vir die ondersteuning wat U vir my gegee het….(Thank you, Lord, for the support you have given me.) VO4: Having been arrested in early February 2023, Frik and Peter are now home. They were released after years of negotiations at every possible level, and their OWN story - told on television for the first time – suggests they paid a brutal price for a vendetta that had nothing to do with them. PAUSE VO5: It began with the arrest and quickly snowballed. Peter Huxham: When we arrived in the courthouse, we knew, I can't tell you how we knew somebody would be endangered by that. But we knew, so we had the knowledge that this is a diplomatic event. Pause VO6 The diplomatic event Peter is referring to unfolded ten years before their imprisonment. Another South African, Daniel Janse van Rensburg, was arrested after a business deal with a relative of the President’s son went sour. He was thrown into Black Beach where he would spend four years before his release. Years later, Janse van Rensburg successfully sued, and assets in Cape Town belonging to Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo’s son were attached by the court. PAUSE It’s here that the seeds were sown for Peter and Frik’s ordeal. PAUSE It’s believed they were used as bargaining chips for the return of those assets which included two luxury houses. Pause VO7 The court found Frik and Peter guilty of TRAFFICKING AND THE ILLICIT POSSESSION OF DRUGS and their more than 24 months in prison began, first being sent to Black Beach. Frik Potgieter: Toe ons daar aan kom en die staldeur nou oopmaak, (When we arrived there, and they opened the steel door,) toe's daar seker, ek skat tussen twee en driehonderd mense daar binne-in. (an estimated 200 or 300 people were inside.) Peter Huxham: One of the guards. He took us to one side. He said, You just need to be calm. You need to try and not show any fear. Frik: Toe’t ek geskrik. Toe sceme ek ek gaan nie môre oggend hier uitkom nie. (That’s when I got a fright. I thought, “Tomorrow, I’m not going to come out of here.) Dis my laaste aand hierso. (This is my last night here.”) VO8 But worse was yet to come. LINK: From notorious Black Beach Peter and Frik were moved to another high security prison. They were blindfolded and handcuffed and taken to what they called the hole. VO9 The prison in an area called Mongomo, while not as well-known as Black Beach, was arguably more sinister – housing political prisoners and criminals of the worst kind. PAUSE VO10 The men spent 6 weeks in solitary confinement. Frik Potgieter - Die selle is baie klein. Die ligte brand permanent in die selle. (The cells are very small. The lights are permanently on.) Daarso is niks indication van of dit dag of nag is nie.(There is… no indication of day or night.) VO11 The months came and went PAUSE UPS: Kathy McConnachie: We haven’t spoken to our men in months. Sonja Potgieter: Yah please, if you can just help us. PAUSE VO12 Back in South Africa their families lobbied the government and parliament. They wrote letters, staged silent protests, and drew attention to their cause on social media. UPS: We’re going to use Parliamentary diplomacy to do what’s needed in this case. VO13 In June last year, the United Nations declared Peter and Frik ‘s incarceration a human rights violation. Frik Potgieter: Dit het vir ons baie hoop gegee en baie moed gegee. (It gave us a lot of hope and courage) Ons het nog steeds aan die een kant getwyfel, want wat gaan die UN vir EG doen?(We still had our doubts, because what can the UN do to EG?) PAUSE UPS: Sonja Potgieter: Hier is die eerste boek wat ek geskryf het. VO14 Frik’s wife, Sonja, kept a diary to record things she could no longer share with him. Sonja Potgieter: Ons het nie geweet hoe lank hy daar gaan wees nie (We didn’t know how long he was going to be there.) So ek het begin skryf vir hom…ek het nou al 5 boeke vol geskryf. (So, I started writing to him…I have written 5 books already) Erin: Het dit jou gehelp? (Did that help you?) Sonja: Dis al hoe dit my gehelp het om hom net te begin vertel van die dag (It’s the only thing that helped me, to tell him about my day.) want dan voel dit vir my asof ek met hom praat. (That made me feel like I was talking to him.) VO15 the men were allowed only a handful of phone calls. Frik: Dit was seker tien, vyf minute die oproep. (It was probably ten- or five- minute phone calls.) Maar ons het amper meer gehuil as wat ons gepraat het. (But we cried more than talked.) SHORT PAUSE Erin: 16;47;28 Wat het jy die meeste gemis van die huis af? (What did you miss most about home?) Frik: Om 'n deur te kan oopmaak en te kan uitstap, buite toe. (To open a door and walk outside.) Ja, en human, human interaction. Net 'n drukkie of 'n smile of wat ook al. (Yes, and human interaction. Just a hug or a smile or something.) PAUSE UPSound: Sonja: Dit klop so vinning want jy is in hegtenis geneem. (It’s beating so fast. You have been arrested.) Wat nou, hoekom? (What now? Why?) Maar ek is dankbaar dis verby. (But I’m thankful it’s over) Ons is deur alles. (We went through it all). PAUSE UPSound: Peter: I wish I was there to just hold you and tell you: “We’ll be ok and that we will all as a family get through this”. VO16 Kathy McConnachie has been with Peter for 32 years. Kathy: My first main concern was his health. Because I knew he depended on his antidepressant and if he didn’t have those he wouldn’t manage. Peter Huxham: It was extremely difficult. I mean, it got to a point where I lost control. VO17 Medication did eventually arrive, but Peter still had very bad days. Peter: And it got to a point where in November, I had blood running down my face from banging my head on the cell door, and the supervisors were shouting at each other. What are they going to do? VO18 Ironically, because it seemed certain Peter and Frik were being used as political pawns, their captors needed to keep them in reasonable health. Peter; They eventually got me to the infirmary, and I think that's still when I said to the supervisor, just kill me now. Just kill me. Erin: And you meant it? Peter Huxham: Yes, absolutely. At that moment in time, I prayed. I prayed, God, take me. UPS protest march VO19 On the 21st of March, South Africa’s Human Rights Day, the families renewed their call for the government to intervene and secure Peter and Frik’s release. PAUSE Three months later they were pardoned. Peter: We just sat there like it's as if all the tension and all the anxiety of the last 28 months just sort of disappeared, and you're just relieved. UP music LINK: It was the moment Peter and Frik had been longing for, to step back on South African soil with their families anxiously waiting for their return. UPSOUND VIDEO Erin: What was it like seeing her? Peter Huxham: Just like nothing else mattered at that moment in time. Just that reconnection and that feeling, this person that you want to share your life with. You can’t live without her. I’ve realised that. Kathy: I was crying. He was as happy as anything and he didn’t stop hugging me ... .and it was part of me that came home. Up music Frik: Toe kon ek, sien ek al die mense buite. ( I saw all the people outside.) Toe sien ek vir Sonja en vir Jolene (I saw Sonja and Jolene.) En toe ek afkom die trappe toe sien ek vir Frickie ook, my seun ook daarso staan. (And when I came down the stairs, I also saw Frikkie - my son - standing there.) Maar dit was overwhelming gewees, ja. (It was overwhelming.) UPS - Frik, Jolene and Sonja in garden with dogs Frik: Ja, so ek weet dis tyd wat mens probeer inhaal wat ek nie kan inhaal nie. (I’m trying to make up for lost time,) Maar om nuwe memories te skep, is al, en tyd te gee. (and to create new memories and to give it time.) UPS Erin: Now that he is home. What are the sweetest moments? Kathy: Oh it is just sitting on the couch watching TV, holding my hand….Kath would you like a cup of coffee? That’s what I missed the most. So it’s Kath, coffee? UPS Peter: I’d love to see this up close almost as much as I would like to see the pyramids. VO21 Peter and Kathy plan to get married in October and then, a long awaited honeymoon in Europe Pause VO22 Frik and Sonja are looking forward to a road trip around the country and Namibia… they won’t go any further north than that. Music up - Peter on bicycle ___________________________________________________________________________ PROMO ONE VO Two South African engineers spent more than 2 years in prison in Equatorial Guinea with no physical contact with family and only a handful of phone calls. Upsound: Frik Potgieter: Toe ons daar aan kom en die staldeur nou oopmaak, (When we arrived there, and they opened the steel door,) toe's daar seker, ek skat tussen twee en driehonderd mense daar binne-in. (an estimated 200 or 300 people were inside.) PROMO TWO VO Locked behind bars in Equatorial Guinea in a confined space they spent two years in prison for a crime they did not commit UPS: Frik Potgieter - Die selle is baie klein. Die ligte brand permanent in die selle.(The cells are small. The lights are permanently on.) Daarso is niks indication van of dit dag of nag is nie. (There is no indication of day or night.) PROMO THREE VO Two South African engineers….now finally home after 864 days in prison in Equatorial Guinea. UPS: Peter Huxham - At that moment in time, I prayed. I prayed, God, take me. I don't want to be here. _____________________________________________________________________________________________

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): After having spent two harrowing years in prison in Equatorial Guinea two innocent South African engineers are finally home. We bring you their story.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: It was the moment Peter Huxham and Frik Potgieter have been waiting for ... .to step back on South African soil at Lanseria Airport where their families have been waiting anxiously. It was an emotional welcome for the two engineers who have not seen their loved ones since their illegal detention in a high security prison in Equatorial Guinea in February 2023. Their release follows a pardon from the President of Equatorial Guinea. This brings an end to a harrowing ordeal of anguish, uncertainty, and unwavering efforts by many to secure their freedom.
metadata.Summary: It is a story of two men who have spent two years and four months in a prison for a crime they did not commit. The emotional, physical and mental toll it took on both Frik and Peter is beyond words. How do you come to terms with the thought that your faith lies in the hands of a government whose judicial system is corrupt? What led to their eventual release was a presidential pardon which proves that they were innocent from the beginning. During those dark days and nights their loved ones lived only in their memory. With the exception of a handful of brief telephone calls, the only connection they had was with the local doctor and their legal representative of the company they worked for. The men lost weight and the worry lines ran deep on their faces. Both are on chronic medication and the poor diet in prison have added to their weight loss. We covered the story of their arrest, sentencing and imprisonment. Now we bring you the story of how the men coped in prison, how their families continued their unfailing support and calling for their release and the eventual release from prison. We take you into the homes of Peter Huxham who, while in prison, proposed to his partner Kathy, who accepted. Kathy, who never gave up hope, washed and ironed Peter’s clothes every week and packed it away for the day he returns. Frik Potgieter’s wife Sonja was part of the support group who sat in countless meetings with DIRCO and on the street during the protest. Timeline: Frik Potgieter and Peter Huxham were arrested in their hotel room in Malabo in Equatorial Guinea on 9 February 2023 on trumped up drug charges and subsequently imprisoned. The two men were arrested two days after South African courts seized the super yacht belonging to the Equatorial Guinean Vice President, and just shortly after two of his Cape Town luxury homes were impounded. The seizures followed a separate court ruling in South Africa that had nothing to do with Frik and Peter. The two men appeared in court on 22 June 2023 charged with illegal drug trafficking. The court case was a farce as no credible evidence, witnesses, or expert testimonies were presented to the court by the State, nor was any proof presented that the alleged drugs were found on Peter or Frik, or that indeed they were drugs. It was alleged that the drugs were found in their luggage, but this was not ture. Their luggage, combination-locked and unopened, was still in their rooms five days later when their employer collected them in the presence of hotel management and the local police. On 29 June 2023 they were found guilty of illegal drug trafficking. Peter and Frik were sentenced each for 12 years in a high security prison in Mongomo, Equatorial Guinea in a prison reserved for political prisoners. They were ordered to pay USD $5 million each in damages, and additional fines to be shared between them. The sentences were based on outdated penalties for the alleged crimes indicating an unsettling departure from the country’s Criminal Code. In July 2024, the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found that their imprisonment was arbitrary, unlawful, and in breach of multiple international human rights obligations. The UN also, at the time, called for their immediate release as their physical and mental health deteriorated, and their families were left in anguish. In October 2024, the South African Parliament passed a unanimous motion demanding urgent action to secure their release. Despite this, Frik and Peter remained in prison in Equatorial Guinea. At the same time the families appealed to the South African government (DIRCO) for urgent intervention and the Presidency to push for Peter and Frik’s release. In a letter to President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, the president of Equatorial Guinea, the families pleaded for clemency. They appealed to him directly as a father and a devout Catholic to have mercy. To support their fight for justice the families turned to social media, calling on the immediate release of Frik and Peter. The petition was signed by 16,000 signatures from around the world. A peaceful protests was staged in Cape Town at the Africa Energy Week which was attended by the South African Minister of International Relations, Minister Ronald Lamola, and his UK counterpart, Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs, the Rt Hon David Lammy to find an urgent solution to Frik and Peter’s ongoing detention in Equatorial Guinea. On Human Rights Day, 21 March 2025 the families continued to call on the government for diplomatic efforts to secure the men’s release from unlawful detention and imploring the President of Equatorial Guinea to grant the men clemency. Then finally, on 21 June 2025 the families of Frik and Peter confirmed that the men have been released and are at home. No media was invited to cover their arrival at Lanseria Airport as there was still a certain amount of doubt that perhaps something could go wrong. Frik and Peter were pardoned by the President of Equatorial Guinea: an act recognising that no crime had been committed by the two men and that they are innocent and their rights should be restored. On the same day of the release a tweet from his son, Teodoro Nguema Obiang, was posted: “Once again, His Excellency the President of the Republic has demonstrated to the world his humanism, solidarity, and reconciliation, the values that embody him, by granting pardons to two South African citizens convicted of drug trafficking”. Peter and Frik’s attorneys in Equatorial Guinea are currently lodging appeals on several issues, including the court process, the verdict, unlawful sentence of imprisonment, and the amounts that they have to pay in damages, fines and legal costs.
